title: Sex differences in the neural circuitry of aggression in Syrian hamsters.
authors: Lee, Susan D; Aspesi, Dario; Huhman, Kim L; Albers, H Elliott
one_liner_zh: 该文研究叙利亚仓鼠攻击行为的神经回路性别差异，采用c-Fos免疫组化，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: The social behavior neural network (SBNN) is a circuit composed of reciprocally connected limbic structures that regulate social behaviors, including aggression. Although both males and females of many species display a range of agonistic behaviors in response to social encounters, studies of the neural circuitry underlying these behaviors have focused almost exclusively on males. In the present study, we investigated sex differences in the neural circuitry activated in response to social interactions in Syrian hamsters (Mesocricetus auratus). We employed c-Fos immunohistochemistry to quantify neuronal activation following agonistic encounters between same-sex male and female dyads during a resident-intruder test. Animals were tested in their home cage either alone (n = 7 per sex) or with a same-sex, non-aggressive intruder (n = 7 per sex) for 10 min. Social interactions were characterized almost exclusively by aggressive interactions with aggression occurring more frequently in females than in males. Our data revealed substantial sex differences in the neuronal activation of the SBNN in response to these encounters. In some regions, neuronal activity changed in opposite directions in males and females compared to controls (e.g., posterior lateral septum), while in others, there was a change in neuronal activation in only one sex (e.g., medial amygdala). These findings support the hypothesis that the neural circuitry activated in response to social interactions including aggression exhibit marked sexual differentiation.
abstract_zh: 社会行为神经网络（SBNN）是由相互连接的边缘结构组成的回路，调节包括攻击行为在内的社会行为。尽管许多物种的雄性和雌性在社交遭遇中都会表现出一系列对抗行为，但针对这些行为背后的神经回路的研究几乎完全集中在雄性上。在本研究中，我们调查了叙利亚仓鼠（Mesocricetus auratus）中响应社交互动而激活的神经回路中的性别差异。我们采用c-Fos免疫组织化学方法，在居住者-入侵者测试中，对同性雄性和雌性配对之间的对抗遭遇后的神经元激活进行了量化。动物在其家庭笼中单独测试（每性别n = 7）或与同性别、非攻击性入侵者（每性别n = 7）进行10分钟测试。社交互动几乎完全以攻击性互动为特征，且攻击行为在雌性中比雄性更频繁发生。我们的数据揭示了SBNN在响应这些遭遇时神经元激活存在显著的性别差异。在某些区域，与对照组相比，雄性和雌性的神经元活动变化方向相反（例如，后外侧隔核），而在其他区域，仅在一个性别中观察到神经元激活的变化（例如，内侧杏仁核）。这些发现支持了以下假设：响应包括攻击行为在内的社交互动而激活的神经回路表现出显著的性别分化。
